text:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 -> AZURE EastAsia: Private DNS multipath failures impacting Private deployments and on-prem egress. >30% of requests to private model endpoints returning 502/504 and long tails. Auto-triggered: runbook v3 (link: https://redir/runbooks/az-eastasia-dns). Notifying on-call.
oncall-sre: acked. I’m online, grabbing context and escalation path.
raj: looking at peering/BGP and Azure private DNS zones now. I see a flurry of asymmetric responses from cluster of Azure DNS servers.
lydia: observed this from our edge: dig @10.1.2.53 model-private.prod.redwood.local A returns two different sets of IPs depending on source ASN. TTLs are fine but responses are inconsistent. dump attached.
maya: customer-facing note: two enterprise Private customers reported timeouts for control-plane RPCs and embedding requests started at ~2339990000. CS pinged both; they're seeing retries/errors in their apps.
sam: quick check — KV-cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 41% around the same time, likely due to upstream failures. Could be cache churn from failing connections.
emily: wondering if this is DNS split-brain from private DNS forwarding between our VPC and on-prem resolvers (we saw similar with a misconfigured conditional forwarder months ago).
oncall-sre: mitigation plan: 1) Fail traffic away from EastAsia for impacted customers via routing-policy override. 2) Short-circuit DNS by pushing explicit A records into our internal service discovery for critical endpoints. 3) Engage Azure support.
raj: running tcpdump on the peering interface to confirm which Azure DNS resolvers are replying. preliminary: instances are replying with different answer sections. Paste from tcpdump:
```
23:11:08.123456 IP 10.1.2.1.53 > 10.1.2.200.57523: Flags [...], udp, length 92
;; -> query id 0x1a2b A model-private.prod.redwood.local
23:11:08.123457 IP 13.107.21.200.53 > 10.1.2.200.57523: Flags [...], udp, length 78
;; -> answer: 10.10.10.45
23:11:08.123458 IP 52.120.45.33.53 > 10.1.2.200.57523: Flags [...], udp, length 78
;; -> answer: 10.20.20.89
```
lydia: that aligns with dig results — different egress paths are getting different authoritative sets. Might be a regional rewrite issue on Azure's side or an L4 NAT inconsistency.
oncall-sre: immediate actions executed: 1) pushed routing-policy override for tenants T-ENT-345 and T-ENT-412 to prefer CentralAsia and fallback to WestAsia clusters (policy id: rp-4612). 2) raised internal DNS override for critical endpoints (TTL 30s) via service discovery: applied patch:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: internal-dns-overrides
data:
  model-private.prod.redwood.local: "10.10.10.45,10.10.10.46"
```
3) increased observability logging on dns-proxy pods.
raj: created Azure support ticket 1900xxxx - case: inconsistent private DNS responses between peering endpoints. Escalated to networking team.
maya: CS update sent: "We're investigating an EastAsia private networking issue causing intermittent timeouts; we've applied temporary routing workarounds and will update within 30 min. If you see continued issues, please escalate to your SE contact."
sam: metric snapshots post-mitigation: request error rate dropped from 6.4% -> 1.9% for affected tenants; latency p95 improved from 2.2s -> 1.1s. KV-cache reclaiming.
emily: can we confirm on-prem resolvers are honoring overrides? I ran `dig model-private.prod.redwood.local @our-resolver` and got the override IPs. Good.
lydia: still seeing some edge nodes get the stale 10.20.20.89 responses — likely cached upstream in some Azure DNS nodes. We should lower TTL and keep overrides until Azure confirms fix.
oncall-sre: agreed. Leaving overrides in place (TTL 30s) and routing-policy until Azure confirms stable state. Opening follow-up: handoff to next on-call in 30m.
raj: next diagnostic: checking peering health and BGP flaps — nothing obvious in BGP session logs, but there are intermittent packet drops to a subset of DNS resolvers. I’ll provide pcap to Azure.
emily: creating an incident doc in ops.incidents with timeline and commands used.
maya: tagging affected customers and scheduling a 1:1 update for enterprise accounts; logging root-cause assumptions: "upstream Azure private DNS resolver inconsistency" until we have confirmation.
oncall-sre: paging status: resolved for now via overrides + routing policy. Keeping P1 open until Azure confirms full resolution and caches flush. Next steps: 1) Azure to confirm fix and TTL propagation, 2) remove overrides and revert routing-policy, 3) postmortem draft.
raj: Azure response: "We see split responses from edge DNS nodes; investigating config propagation delay across private resolvers. No BGP change noted." Case updated.
lydia: recommend we run a controlled rollback test: remove overrides for a small subset of canary hosts and monitor 1/5m error windows. If stable for 15m, widen.
oncall-sre: doing canary rollback now for canary group CG-3.
sam: canary CG-3 steady for 18m, errors at baseline. rolling out rollback to CG-1 (30% traffic).
emily: adding handoff note: next on-call (sam) will follow until Azure closes case. Recording artifacts: tcpdump, dig outputs, config patches, routing-policy id rp-4612.
maya: final customer note draft attached for later: "We applied a temporary routing and DNS override to mitigate an Azure resolver inconsistency. We're working with Azure to validate their fix and will remove temporary measures once stability is confirmed."
oncall-sre: closing loop for this thread — P1 remains open until Azure resolves; handoff complete to sam. If anything new, @sam please escalate. :thumbsup:
